hierarchie: Two boss/Five subordinate: Two bosses will want to know how the subordinate feels personally. The Five may interpret this as an intrusion, especially if the Two boss tries to get the Five subordinate to talk about their life outside the company. The Two boss, especially lacking information about their subordinate's private life, might worry that they are unhappy having to manage alone.

Two boss/Five subordinate: In seeking to be of service, this boss might overstep the boundaries of the personal space that lets the Five function comfortably in their professional environment. The Two should focus their attention on ongoing projects rather than wondering about the Five's emotional life. It would be better to assign Observers specific tasks and, if possible, give them a separate space and let them operate as they see fit.

Two boss/Five subordinate: Bosses will be pleased with the Five's ability to be autonomous and to make decisions alone. Two bosses' attention is often drawn to influential people within the company. Fives are subordinates perfectly capable of managing day-to-day business while their Two boss works on growing the company.

Two boss/Five subordinate: The interaction works beautifully when the Five subordinate's job is to usefully inform the extroverted Two boss, who in exchange can spare them too much human contact. If the Five is the boss, the door to the inner sanctum will be politely left ajar for their Two subordinate, but the office will be steeped in an aura of inaccessibility. The Two will feel deprived of a source of presence and exchange.

Five boss/Two subordinate: If the Five shows wisdom, they will make the Helper a special envoy. Helpers are natural intermediaries between the public and those in power. The Five boss might also organize semi-official meetings with each staff member, even if these gatherings do not directly address work matters.

Five boss/Two subordinate: These would be meant only to gather employees' opinions. And since Five bosses are not models of interaction or cooperation, this is no small opportunity to be heard. Fives should also allow group meetings that let employees get to know one another.

Five boss/Two subordinate: The fact that the Five boss is rarely available can leave employees dissatisfied. "Management is never there when you need them." The purpose of these semi-official meetings would be to offer a chance to settle disagreements.
Five boss/Two subordinate: If the Five gives up, the Two might step in on behalf of their boss, who is not really comfortable with confrontation.
Two boss/Five subordinate: Fives are subordinates perfectly capable of managing day-to-day business while their Two boss works on growing the company.
Two boss/Five subordinate: The interaction works beautifully when the Five subordinate's job is to usefully inform the extroverted Two boss, who in exchange can spare them too much human contact.

duos.title: Pair 2–6 (Two and Six)
amour: The Helper-Loyalist couple in love A typical interaction is one in which the Two draws close to the Six to neutralize the Six's fear of too much intimacy. The Six's doubt can become a catalyst for the Helper, who loves overcoming obstacles to the relationship.
The message conveyed will be: "Believe in me." In the early stages, the Two comes to help their skeptical partner, and the Six learns to feel secure through this attention.

It helps when the Helper supports the cause of the underdog, which matters so much to the Six partner. The Six can then come to trust the Two's intentions, since the Two goes to such trouble for a good cause.

It may prove harder to lead the Loyalist toward personal success. Fearing to become a recognized authority, the Six may view the Two's help as self-serving and, ever skeptical, wonder whether the Helper isn't there to take advantage of the situation.

The Six may feel manipulated and get the impression of serving the Two's ambitions. Already stressed by success and public attention, the Six might sabotage the Two's efforts by failing to meet their expectations.

The Six finds themselves caught in a bind: on one hand, flattered by the Two's care and attention, and on the other, frustrated at doubting the sincerity of their intentions. The Six might also feel that too much is expected of them and might rebel.

Frustrated in turn at not seeing the fruits of their efforts materialize, the Two will start openly criticizing the Six's halting progress toward their goals. Mutual mistrust can ease if the Six manages to separate their own goals from those the Two has for them, and gives priority to their own.

The Six should try to be more physically demonstrative and to accept the Two's sincere affection instead of mistaking their natural warmth for flattery. It is essential that the Two sort out whether the help they offer is altruistic or self-interested.
The Six's doubt risks uncovering the Two's unconscious aim of giving in order to receive. Once secure, the Six can prove devoted in the support they give to family life.
Besides, it is always better for the Two to choose their own profession and activities.
travail: Here is another pairing built on differences.
Twos are drawn to power, and Sixes are ambivalent about holding authority.
This is a natural alliance in a difficult context, such as restructuring a company or organizing a contested grassroots movement.
Both profiles lead well when they can act in accordance with their convictions.
Twos flourish when worthwhile projects appear, and Sixes identify with the efforts to be made.
Conflicts will eventually arise in a "normal" workplace, where self-interest and competition show up rather than healthy collaboration.
Both types are liable to falter if they hold a leadership position for too long.
Sixes because of the stress brought on by the performance-driven aspects of point Three, and Twos because they want to be appreciated.
Six bosses will want assurance of their subordinates' loyalty and will be unsettled if Twos change their attitude to please a rival who holds some power.
hierarchie: Six boss/Two subordinate: The Two's social instincts will lead them to draw the attention of "whoever is worth the trouble," and this will arouse the Loyalist's suspicions. The Six boss will tell themselves: "How far can I trust this employee?
Six boss/Two subordinate: Can I entrust them with confidential information?" Both profiles may feel targeted by latent animosity within the company.

Six boss/Two subordinate: Six bosses will try to find the source of the problem in order to fix it; Twos will try to make friends. A Two subordinate may read their Six boss's hesitations as an evasion of responsibility.

Six boss/Two subordinate: Doubting minds unsettle Helpers, since Twos are used to direct relationships; and Sixes take a long time before granting their trust. Twos may also become aware of the Six boss's potential, but if their abilities fail to show themselves, the Two subordinate will feel threatened and will look elsewhere for a more appealing working relationship.
Six boss/Two subordinate: Loyalists want to appear egalitarian. They will find it unfair to "manipulate" an employee to get better productivity out of them.
Six boss/Two subordinate: By failing to give the Two particular attention, the Six boss passes up a fine opportunity. The Two, to function, needs their talent for influence to be acknowledged.

Two boss/Six subordinate: Six subordinates see problems coming from far off, and the Two boss will thus be able to fend off danger using their own political talents. If Sixes think Two bosses are selfish and therefore dangerous, Twos will have to face possible opposition building behind the scenes aimed at challenging their authority.

Six boss/Two subordinate: Twos may also become aware of the Six boss's potential, but if their abilities fail to show themselves, the Two subordinate will feel threatened and will look elsewhere for a more appealing working relationship.
Six boss/Two subordinate: Loyalists want to appear egalitarian.
Six boss/Two subordinate: They will find it unfair to "manipulate" an employee to get better productivity out of them.

duos.title: Pair 2–7 (Two and Seven)
amour: The Helper-Epicure couple in love This combination can prove quite delightful. Twos will want to help Epicures reach their goals, and they will share the Seven's enthusiasm for the relationship. The Seven's vision often forms the foundation of the couple's emotional life. The partners will nurture hope for a bright shared future.

Both profiles have very diverse interests: Twos, because of their multiple personalities, and Sevens, because of their multi-option thinking. The couple is drawn to the best shows and to everything making headlines. Helpers will be very attentive to the Seven's promising talents, but will also perceive their hidden sorrows. Twos are fascinated by the Seven's radiant surface and doubly attracted by the fact that they are dissatisfied underneath.

Nonetheless, Helpers often interpret the Seven's appetite for experience as a search for deep emotion. Twos understand that Sevens need to focus their attention. Helpers may feel called to coach Sevens toward greater productivity and to heal their underlying fears. Helpers find themselves rewarded by the adventure and by the attention Sevens give them.

Sevens make charming partners and can even represent a romantic ideal. Both profiles tend toward optimism. The Seven's charm combined with the Two's alluring side produces an attractive couple. Sevens are preoccupied with themselves and, whether or not their partner is present, will act in their own interest.

Twos will take care of their multiple personalities rather than wait at home doing nothing. Both like to stay active and always thirst for novelty. Commitment is possible for Sevens if they do not feel confined. People embodying these two profiles are seductive by nature.

Each enjoys weighing the other's potential availability. It is advisable to stabilize the relationship through mutual commitments and to determine the degree of outside attention each one needs. Both profiles are wary of prolonged contact: Sevens fear it will become confining, and Twos fear it will eventually expose them. Sevens escape into pleasurable activities.

Twos see this as a challenge and follow Sevens into their adventures. But Twos often need more attention than Sevens can give them. Twos tell themselves: "Our plans seem to change so easily. Will my partner keep his intentions toward me?"

A crisis can arise: the Two discovering the lightness and superficiality of their partner, and the Seven starting to view the Two as an emotional burden. If the Two insists on receiving more attention, the Seven will eventually think: "That was never part of the deal." The couple is united in optimism: each wants to be told that life will be beautiful. They would need to build on genuine feelings rather than on ideas.
The couple should unite through the adventure of moving from fascination to deep emotional feeling.
Twos understand that Sevens need to focus their attention.
travail: This pairing is a classic in the professional world.
When Sevens have ideas, Twos bring them to life.
In the best of cases, the Seven's visionary faculties will be served by the Two's talent as a stage manager.
Unfortunately, they may be unable to carry a project through to a happy conclusion.
Epicures perform well in a project's early stages and then lose their enthusiasm.
Helpers, for their part, are effective when they can support a leader who delivers tangible results.
hierarchie: Seven boss/Two subordinate: Two subordinates serving Seven bosses might want to do too much, hoping to meet their needs. Sevens may only think out loud, and Twos may end up overloaded with work and ignored.
Seven boss/Two subordinate: It is rare for Sevens to be powerful leaders. If Twos notice this and feel neglected on top of it, they will try to find a more enviable situation elsewhere.

Seven boss/Two subordinate: Twos do not waste time with someone who does not appreciate them. If Sevens have narcissistic preoccupations and Twos are dissatisfied, none of the Epicure's grand plans will come to fruition.

Seven boss/Two subordinate: If plans keep changing and goals are not met, Twos will feel ineffective. Without a personal bond to hold them, Two subordinates will find another position within the company.

Seven boss/Two subordinate: Dissatisfied, they will maneuver to find a face-saving way out. The Two boss should give the Seven subordinate tasks that spare them boredom: the Seven works well as long as they are learning something or have a challenge to meet.

Two boss/Seven subordinate: If that is not the case, the Two boss may find that they cannot rely on the Seven and will worry about output and deadlines. They might also feel their authority is threatened: "What will my superiors think if he keeps doing just as he pleases?", "How can I keep him under control while still keeping him happy?"

Two boss/Seven subordinate: In doubt, the Two will either draw closer to their subordinate and become their friend, or pull away and cut ties. For the sake of both profiles, the Two boss should spell out the consequences of such behavior.
Two boss/Seven subordinate: The Seven's charm and their positive reframing will vanish in the face of a clear deadline.
Seven boss/Two subordinate: Dissatisfied, they will maneuver to find a face-saving way out.
Two boss/Seven subordinate: The Two boss should give the Seven subordinate tasks that spare them boredom: the Seven works well as long as they are learning something or have a challenge to meet.

duos.title: Pair 2–8 (Two and Eight)
amour: The Helper-Protector couple in love This couple rests on the Two's charm and the Eight's strength. The Two moves toward others to try to please, and the Eight moves against others to uncover the truth. Both profiles want to be at the heart of their partner's life. Both demand attention, but their means of obtaining it are radically different.

The Two adapts their feelings to the other's needs, and the Eight insists that their own desires be satisfied. Since the Eight is sexually expressive, and Twos do not clearly distinguish between love and sexuality, physical attention will matter greatly in the relationship. The Eight's plans will sit at the center of the agenda. Their desires demand satisfaction, and the Two makes it a point of honor that the other's desires come true.

The most common interaction shows the Two trying to soften the Eight, and the Eight resisting these efforts. This produces a certain attraction that can persist for years. The "self-referencing" Eight will receive a great deal of attention, and the Two, being other-centered, is thereby spared having to let their own needs surface. In return for the help Twos offer, Eights will provide vigorous protection and their natural leadership.

Following the arrows of the Enneagram, a secure Eight can move toward a more empathetic Two-like stance. That does not mean Eights "become Twos" when they feel secure; they simply express the Two's need for attention in their own Eight way. They do so either by controlling the Two's life, or by effectively helping them reach their goals. Eights more rarely give up control by allowing Twos to take charge of the relationship's future.

An Eight at point Two can be very generous. He proves his affection by contributing to his partner's projects. This puts the Two in the uncomfortable position of having to receive, and can give them the impression of being dominated by the Eight, even when the support offered is entirely legitimate. If the Two is able to center on themselves, discover their needs, and try to get what they truly want, the Eight may be willing to give up the lead.

But if the Two is afraid their personal needs will be exposed, or if the Eight dominates too strongly, the Two will implode, fight for their freedom, and slide into their stress point at Eight. Many Two-Eight couples claim that conflicts can have the constructive effect of bringing them closer. But there are also cases where Twos feel they have been used. They gave everything and were not appreciated.

Now they want revenge. Conflicts between enraged Twos and their ex-Eight partners can escalate into open warfare. A meeting at point Eight can trigger intense animosity between partners. Twos at point Eight can prove to be dangerous manipulators.

Not accustomed to direct confrontation, they may resort to other means such as personal influence, rumor, or social pressure. Twos want to keep their image intact and will therefore present their ex-partners as solely responsible. If Twos are wounded in their pride or openly rejected, they may air their grievances publicly and dramatically. A dispute traditionally shows the Eight, feeling betrayed by emotionally manipulative games, growing increasingly combative.
His attitude says: "You're being dishonest, don't play games with me!"
This produces a certain attraction that can persist for years.
travail: Trust is the key word here.
When each relies on the other's intentions, they are capable of acting in near-perfect harmony.
Two and Eight share the same axis of the Enneagram, and at work this shows up as Eights playing the role of bosses and Twos acting as intermediaries between them and the staff.
In this way they can illustrate "good cop and bad cop," the Protector laying down the law and the Helper making concessions.
This pairing can prove fruitful if the Two receives enough attention and the Eight feels secure enough to release some of their control.
hierarchie: Two boss/Eight subordinate: Two bosses will need to earn the Eight's support. Eight subordinates, demanding about the quality of leadership, will likely scrutinize the Two's popularity closely.

Two boss/Eight subordinate: "Is management really loyal?" or "Doesn't this director only think of himself?" The Two's inclination to favor people who "are worth it" may look disloyal to Eights, who care deeply about fairness.

Two boss/Eight subordinate: Alarmed by possible injustices within the company, Eights will simply try to eliminate as many controls as possible. If tensions rise, the Two boss may find themselves at a disadvantage against the Eight.

Two boss/Eight subordinate: The Eight is not there to find a face-saving solution, and having no popularity to defend, can become especially irritating to a profile that values its image. It is recommended that limits be defined and the consequences of overstepping them be clearly known, both to management and to employees; agreements should also be clearly written down.

Two boss/Eight subordinate: Deprived of internal rules, the Eight subordinate may feel threatened and refuse to cooperate fully: "Why are all the advantages on management's side? Maybe they're hiding something from us.
Two boss/Eight subordinate: Let's take a closer look!" Eight bosses will be either adored or hated by their Two subordinates.

Eight boss/Two subordinate: If they are loved, the Two's natural tendency to want approval from authority will assure Eights of loyal support. Two subordinates will need to take care to provide detailed reports.
Eight boss/Two subordinate: When information does not reach them right away, Eights can suspect a conspiracy. Subordinates should even deliver far more information than is strictly needed.

Eight boss/Two subordinate: It would also be good for Eight bosses to entrust subordinates with research and investigation missions. That way, Helpers will be flattered to feel indispensable, and Eights will retain control.

Eight boss/Two subordinate: If the Two-Eight pairing does not click, Twos will tend to deprive bosses of useful contacts and information, and will find comfort within a small team of their own personal making.

duos.title: Pair 2–9 (Two and Nine)
amour: The Helper-Mediator couple in love The partners in this couple can seem alike. Both claim to adopt the other's goals, absorb their partner's emotions, and devote themselves to meeting their needs. Even though these two profiles merge emotionally, their motivations differ.

Nines seek a reason to live, which they can find in their partner, while Twos try to find an identity through the other. As these two partners merge, each can be deeply affected by the other on a nonverbal level. Helpers want to help Nines find a purpose.

They will certainly be useful if Nines have the abilities needed to excel in a field that will flatter Twos. The latter may also be drawn to the goodness and kindness Nines frequently display. Mediators appreciate the affection given them, which allows Twos to be as expansive as they wish.

Each of these profiles can use sexuality to spark real contact, and Twos often feel that sexual attention is in fact love. Sexuality can serve as a metaphor for the best a Two-Nine couple's partners have to offer each other. The Two asks: "What do you want?" The Nine answers: "I want you, as you truly are."

The Nine is able to help the Two tell the difference between a self adapted to circumstances and an authentic emotional self, while the Two is able to stir the Nine's eroticism. A crisis can arise if the Two becomes indispensable and the Nine feels controlled. The Mediator will suspect their Two partner of trying to meet unacknowledged needs and will stubbornly refuse to cooperate.

The Nine, to get revenge, will hold back their own potential and direct their attention elsewhere. The Two will grow tired of seeing the Nine accomplish nothing and will be furious at no longer being able to hold their attention. The Two will not appreciate having to take the lead in the couple, since they much prefer to be inspired and led by their partner.

Feeling abandoned because of the Nine's lack of initiative, the Two will start complaining. A painful cycle can set in: the Nine backs away from the Two's demands, who then insists all the more, pushing the Mediator to retreat into sulky silence. If the Nine digs in or fails to tap into their potential, the Two will want to reclaim their freedom.

Fearing separation, the Nine wakes up but can also become possessive. If the Nine tries to draw closer, the Two will pull back, loudly demanding their freedom. The Nine may also choose to lose interest in the situation, which will prompt the Two to want to restore contact.

This deadlock can end if the Two goes back to taking care of their partner's needs. Nines would do well to concern themselves with their own affairs rather than contest others' goals. Twos, for their part, should know that Nines take time before deciding.
They make major decisions only as a last resort. Twos could raise a question, negotiate a deadline, and, in the meantime, leave Nines in peace.
travail: This pairing can project the image of a boost given to activating a source of energy. Helpers spring into action for the benefit of others, and Mediators need to be stimulated.
This alliance is common, both among married couples and in professional life. It produces excellent results provided the partners' goals coincide.

The Nine holds the goal to be reached but has managed to bury it under masses of secondary projects. This goal is so wonderful that the Nine does not feel up to it and, lacking the ideal, settles for less.

The Two's genius lies in their ability to meet needs, to bring hopes to fruition, and to reveal to others their own potential. If the goals coincide, the Two activates the Nine's energy and propels them toward their goal.
The Two sets about structuring the Nine's potential, and the Nine is carried by the energy and attention given them. The partners' pace is very different.
Twos will grow impatient with the time spent making easy decisions. Twos find it easier than Nines to set priorities.

When Two bosses are confronted with the Nine's work rhythm, the Mediator's sometimes leisurely tempo grows tiresome for them. Meanwhile, Two subordinates have little patience for the repeated discussions and meetings so often favored by Nine bosses.
As the two profiles merge, nonverbal communication comes easily. Both are concerned with the atmosphere within their company.

Nines register others' emotional distress, will want to hear every opinion, and are attentive to defusing potential conflicts. Twos excel at spotting promising talent and placing it in strategic positions within the company.
The partners' pace is very different.
hierarchie: Two boss/Nine subordinate: As bosses, Twos are more interested in developing high-potential staff than in rigorous structures. They work to build a supportive company that thrives on the human warmth found there.
Two boss/Nine subordinate: They will benefit from the Nine's knowledge of everyone's viewpoints. They will also appreciate the fact that Nines, as subordinates, will rarely try to take their place.

Two boss/Nine subordinate: Nines are generally loyal to a caring boss, and Twos, in return, know how to publicly recognize their employees' merits, which motivates Nines to surpass themselves. Two bosses generally have their favorites.

Two boss/Nine subordinate: In their dealings with authority, Nines rely on structure and may feel unequal treatment. If the Two boss invites the Nine into their circle of favorites, the Nine subordinate risks turning a deaf ear rather than accepting.

Two boss/Nine subordinate: On the other hand, if the Nine subordinate is not among the chosen few, their inner anger can become a source of trouble with management. The Two boss can make up for it by apologizing and entrusting them with a medium-term mission.

Two boss/Nine subordinate: Generally, Nines adapt and become cooperative following a conflict. Nine bosses are effective when the path forward is clearly laid out, and in that case, they will receive Twos' full support.

Nine boss/Two subordinate: Two subordinates can help their Nine boss by summarizing the range of opinions expressed within the company, pointing out politically sound courses of action, helping them get past the difficulty of decision-making, and building them a career plan.
Two boss/Nine subordinate: If the Two boss invites the Nine into their circle of favorites, the Nine subordinate risks turning a deaf ear rather than accepting.
Two boss/Nine subordinate: On the other hand, if the Nine subordinate is not among the chosen few, their inner anger can become a source of trouble with management.
Two boss/Nine subordinate: The Two boss can make up for it by apologizing and entrusting them with a medium-term mission.

duos.title: Pair 3–3 (Three and Three)
amour: A couple of Achievers in love This couple is a rare species. There are relatively few Threes at our Enneagram workshops, and couples of Threes are rarer still there. Achievers are found more often at professional events, and when they take an interest in the Enneagram, it is most often to apply it in their professional life.

Threes feel drawn to every point on the Enneagram. Some are attracted to "similar" types, energetic and rather extroverted, like Twos and Sevens. Other Threes are drawn instead to highly emotional partners like Fours, whom they see as a complement.

As an example, and based on my experience in California, the most common pairing is a Three with a Five, with Achievers explaining this pairing by the fact that the differences balance each other out. The rare couples of Threes I have met told me they appreciated their mutual liveliness. Everything seems possible to them, and they generally have several projects underway.

They admit to growing impatient often and to tending to compete with each other when it comes to running the household. This may be the reason each maintains, on their own side, all sorts of professional connections. Their social life consists of spending time with people who share similar professional concerns, or with parents whose children attend the same schools and who also enjoy dynamic activities.

Their social orientation is, moreover, unmistakably active. This is a couple that does a great many things together and that is drawn closer by shared activities rather than dull family gatherings. The ideal is to support each other's achievements without falling into the trap of leading separate lives while living under the same roof.

This couple can give the illusion that all is well, with every appearance of happiness and prosperity, yet lacking inner intensity and solid emotional bonds. Threes admit that relationships can seem perfect while being empty of meaning. They can take interest in and grow enthusiastic about projects, yet develop indifference regarding their future.
"A new challenge? Do we have to rally our forces again?" These couples say they have felt an emotional numbing that dulls the satisfaction of tasting the fruits of their efforts.

There is a need to hurry, to get things done quickly, and to move on without pause to new projects. All of this seems normal, well organized, and promising of worthwhile results, but, over time, it becomes clear that something is missing. It is a feeling similar to what Sevens often describe on reaching their forties: "What is there left to do that we haven't already done?"

Weariness with the outer world generally triggers the need to turn toward one's inner life and to deepen one's emotions. From that point on, projects and professional contacts start to feel superficial. From there, if the efforts poured into their careers are not accompanied by feelings and a willingness to be touched by emotion, they will become increasingly aware that something vital is missing.
A relationship between two Threes can either reinforce their belief that feelings and professional success are incompatible, or give them good reason to turn toward their inner life.
travail: Threes are highly valued in start-ups. They generally love sales and marketing, and their enthusiasm can prove to be a company's best advertisement. They have a natural affinity for fast-moving, dynamic businesses.

A new and promising project is Three territory. Difficulties can arise when Threes must outdo one another. They flourish in a work environment that offers challenges, but if the promotion system pits them against each other, they will clash.

Threes work to land bonuses, not so much for the financial payoff as because their psychological well-being depends on their successes. They are more vulnerable than others to professional failure and will guard against the pain of losing status. Outside job opportunities will be quietly explored.

Threes are always ready to jump ship. They may keep contacts and potential clients in reserve, hide them, and cash them in later. Their competitive spirit can resemble the selfish attitude of someone who wants to win at all costs, when in fact the Three is often simply in the process of increasing their market value.

One should be able to entrust the Three with full responsibility for a piece of work in their field and encourage them to share information by setting an example of effective collaboration that values both successes and team effort. Two Threes working together can form an unbeatable duo when their goals coincide. This is a dynamic pairing that will certainly move the business forward, if it is humanly possible to do so.

Their ideas are similar, which is both a blessing and a curse. They can make things move, but they may also, unfortunately, do so superficially. Polarized by doubt and failure, Threes can react too quickly to an imminent threat: they might want to change course to secure short-term profits without thinking through the consequences enough.

Threes are contrarians who can kick against the traces during a phase of company consolidation. There can be times when budget cuts and other such measures prove useful, but Threes may interpret these as failures. When policy changes occur within the company and controversial or unpopular decisions are called for, or when meticulous long-term planning is needed, Achievers are not in their element.
They are more vulnerable than others to professional failure and will guard against the pain of losing status.
Outside job opportunities will be quietly explored.
Threes are always ready to jump ship.
hierarchie: Three boss: The Three boss will need to set the example of what they expect from their Three subordinate.
Three boss: Threes take on the prevailing style and will imitate whatever model is deemed optimal in their work environment.
Three boss: If collaboration is the norm, Threes will collaborate to the best of their ability.
Three boss: If personal exploits are rewarded, those same Threes could become formidable competitors.
Three subordinate: Three subordinates seek positions that let them grow.
Three subordinate: It would help if these were clearly defined, so that Threes have no need to maneuver and scheme to get what they want.
Three subordinate: To work better with Threes, one should make sure their merits are recognized, while avoiding putting them in competition with other employees.

Three subordinate: The company should promote team spirit rather than competition; its structure should rest on the principle of effective collaboration rather than on a hierarchical system built on personal power.

duos.title: Pair 3–4 (Three and Four)
amour: The Achiever–Romantic couple in love Both profiles attach supreme importance to their image and to the attention others pay them. Achievers want their accomplishments respected, and Romantics need to be seen as unique. The couple generally presents well and often adopts an elegant lifestyle that projects an image of success.

Threes are first drawn to the inner drama of Fours, which strikes them as the counterpart of their own desire for recognition. For Fours, the Three's interest in the goods of this world can also be stimulating. Achievers always seem preoccupied with their work, even in moments of intimacy.

This drift of attention can irritate Fours, who have a great need for intimate contact. The Achiever's inclination toward professional pursuits can also create a mechanism of psychological distancing that can prove attractive. Four partners never seem to get enough attention from Threes, which leads them to focus on the best aspects of whatever seems to be missing.
Here is an example of the differing viewpoints of such a couple. Dreams A Three with a Four My wife and I are driving through Santa Fe at sunset. The sight is sumptuous — it feels like paradise.
Three hundred and sixty degrees of shimmering colors dotted with a few patches of green. We stop at the edge of the overlook above the city. It is simply dazzling.

We hold hands and the lights blaze through the windshield. I suddenly hear her say through a sob: "We will never live a moment like this again, and to think it will soon be over!" At the very same instant, I realize I am busy working out a whole plan for us each to take a second job so we can buy a plot of land on a hillside… The moods of Fours and the suspended feelings of Threes are at the root of the couple's main difficulties.

It is classic in this kind of relationship: Fours go starved for affection while Threes swear to devote more time to them and rarely keep their promises. Fours will find it hard to picture a couple's life with only minimal intimacy. The unavailability of Threes can prove magnetizing, because the couple does not spend enough time together for the relationship to feel ordinary.

Deprived of intimacy, Fours slip into dramatics, recrimination, or depression — all emotional demands that Threes detest. Fours overvalue emotional life, while Threes undervalue it. A crisis can arise when Fours go to great lengths to hold the Three's attention, and the Three responds by delaying things and overloading their schedule with activities.

Each would need to gain access to the other's view of the world. For instance, Threes claim to demonstrate the value of their commitment by working "for the couple." Fours could try to understand this "non-emotional" way of loving, and distinguish between an overload of work meant to numb feelings and a mass of work meant to prove commitment.

The Three wants to look their best in the eyes of loved ones, so the Four's dissatisfaction can seriously undermine the Three's self-esteem. Rather than retaliate by trivializing the Four's yearnings, or feeling insufficiently appreciated for "all the work I've put in for the two of us," the Three should instead lean into the Four's fascination with what feels missing. Learning to feel the whole range of emotion the Four moves through could take a lifetime of work, but the effort would make the relationship deeply rewarding rather than merely happy.
travail: Here again is a juxtaposition of differences that can result either in a fruitful collaboration or a disastrous experience at work.
With their driving energy, Threes deliver substantial output, while the output of Fours is more refined than easy.
The combination works well when Fours are appreciated for an original, even controversial contribution that ultimately comes to be seen as a success thanks to the backing of Threes.
If the two profiles end up in competition, trouble begins.
Each seeks recognition, and their rivalry can go so far as to ruin everything rather than make a concession.
hierarchie: Three boss/Four subordinate: The Three boss may act "for show." The Four subordinate will notice the difference between what they do that is useful and what they do purely for appearances. The Three boss, assuming employees must devote themselves to their tasks regardless of their feelings, should write in red ink in their daily planner: "Don't raise your voice" and "Ask for their agreement."

Three boss/Four subordinate: Threes have a marked preference for creative productivity and can be captivated by people who emphasize authentic, useful work. It can seem presumptuous to want work to reflect the personality of whoever does it, rather than simply meeting the plain requirements of a job. Fours would rather hold back for years than accept the security of an uninspiring job.

Three boss/Four subordinate: This insistence on being able to personify one's work is the opposite of the Three's willingness to submit to grinding, mind-numbing work, provided it promises to move them up the ladder. Every Three boss encourages subordinates toward any creative idea that could boost productivity or speed the company's development. Four bosses can be unsettled by open competition from a Three.

Four boss/Three subordinate: The partners can work in concert as long as Threes stay busy, but they can clash if Achievers start wanting to impress the hierarchy and staff. Fours in positions of authority tend to see Threes as clumsy. However smart they may be, they lack style.

Four boss/Three subordinate: It's like the look a high-fashion model might give a slightly trashy schoolgirl: "Ridiculous! And how vulgar, showing off like that!" But any boss trying to block an ambitious Three should expect them to use roundabout means.

Four boss/Three subordinate: These Three subordinates will simply grab the ball, sidestep the boss, and try to reach their goal with the help of the ruling elite. Bringing in a third party helps make Three–Four relationships more fruitful. The Three must accept that it is necessary to respect the social barriers separating them from the Four boss.

Four boss/Three subordinate: Through its interventions, the third party should dispel the impression that the Three is nothing but a reckless opportunist, and confirm the Four's hierarchical superiority. The Three subordinate will be encouraged to respect their lesser position in the company if their superior has the confidence of the hierarchy. Besides, Threes are impressed by models of success, and they will collaborate all the more effectively when the org chart is clear.
Three boss/Four subordinate: Every Three boss encourages subordinates toward any creative idea that could boost productivity or speed the company's development.
Four boss/Three subordinate: Four bosses can be unsettled by open competition from a Three.
Four boss/Three subordinate: The partners can work in concert as long as Threes stay busy, but they can clash if Achievers start wanting to impress the hierarchy and staff.

duos.title: Pair 3–5 (Three and Five)
amour: The Achiever–Observer couple in love Threes generally see themselves as extroverted, and Fives, for the most part, fit the definition of introversion. The introvert's need for privacy poses a challenge for Achievers, whose good image rests on recognition of their accomplishments. The differences in nature between the two push the Three to draw closer to their more emotionally guarded partner and to take charge of the practical side of domestic life. For instance, if a trip is being planned, the Three will gather brochures, suggest an itinerary, and handle the reservations.

The Five need only pack their bag. This pairing is very common, both in love and at work, and it generally starts with the Three moving toward the emotionally distant Five. The Three will show their affection by devoting time and energy to the solitary partner who needs it so much. Fives have quite a bit of difficulty committing to an emotional relationship.

It is so easy for Fives to stay detached and let things drift that their mere recurring presence amounts to a de facto commitment. They often take the initiative in a relationship by arranging for the other person to make the first move. Threes will have to restrain themselves from entering the Five's security perimeter too quickly — rushing in would only send the Five back into their shell. Fives prove their availability tacitly, by revealing things about themselves, by devoting energy to keeping up the household, and, above all, by being present.

Nonverbal communication works well in this kind of couple. In case of mutual attraction, the Three, unless checked in their momentum, goes forward, and the Five commits simply by their presence. These differences in psychological makeup form the pivot of this relationship. The Three's need for social relationships will be counterbalanced by the Five's desire for privacy.

In the most common arrangement, the Three becomes the couple's "social secretary." The Three screens phone calls and sorts through invitations, discusses them with the Five in private, and then relays the answer to whoever is concerned. Family life may take the form of two parallel, jointly agreed-upon stories, in which the partners each go their own way and only meet at set times for meals and family activities. Contrary to what one might expect, it is often the Fives who protest against their Three partner's repeated absences.

Once attached, Fives may want to enjoy the security of their territory and, like Eights, want to restrict their partner's outings. Threes then cut back their work hours to keep the peace at home, and only gradually resume multiplying their professional commitments afterward. This can produce a cyclical crisis in which Fives sulk and withhold comfort, presence, and sex, while Threes bury themselves in work waiting for the difficult moment to pass. When Threes feel threatened, they generally redouble their activity to numb their feelings.

This attitude has the negative effect of increasing the distance separating them from others. Negotiating mutual concessions with a clear head can only benefit such a relationship. Neither partner is really touched by the language of feelings, and intimacy poses problems for both types; Threes fear being disconnected from their accomplishments, and Fives fear exhausting themselves meeting the other's needs. Both partners appreciate shared activities with a predetermined time.

Fives can show their goodwill if they know what to expect, and Threes express themselves through action. The couple may find it easier to talk when their attention is diverted by a round of golf or a walk. Each proves their affection by doing something the other enjoys: Threes through material accomplishments "for the couple," and Fives, more subtly, by giving up some of their personal time. These two independent-natured people should, ideally, work out a system of negotiation that lets each adapt to the other's way of relating.
Fives, for example, could learn to appreciate the pleasures of social life, and Threes to let themselves be touched by silence and delicacy.
They often take the initiative in a relationship by arranging for the other person to make the first move.
travail: This is, in business, one of the most common pairings. Fives typically occupy positions where they analyze situations, while Achievers are put in charge of marketing and human resources.

Fives often supply the underlying ideas and theory, which are then developed and put into action by the Three's energy. Achievers will take the initiative in making contacts and handle thorny matters, thereby shielding Observers from conflict and unpleasant surprises.
Threes want control over whatever, in their partnership with Fives, is visible and serves their image. Thanks to the Three, Fives can develop and market what was only a mental construct.
These partners may have difficulty resolving their communication problems. Both set feelings aside, avoid conflict, and are therefore put off by unpleasant truths.
Threes dress up negative information to protect their image, and Fives may avoid talking about upsetting things. Both profiles react to feelings with a delay.

Threes forget their emotions by working, and Fives take time to discern what they feel. When a difficult problem arises, it helps to break it down into several sub-questions and set dates for a series of meetings to address them.

This approach particularly suits people who like to resolve disagreements methodically rather than emotionally. Fives like to detach and prepare for each stage of a negotiation, and Threes manage to muzzle their feelings through activity.
Both set feelings aside, avoid conflict, and are therefore put off by unpleasant truths.
Threes dress up negative information to protect their image, and Fives may avoid talking about upsetting things.
Both profiles react to feelings with a delay.
hierarchie: Three boss/Five subordinate: The Three boss might wish the Five subordinate, who tends to dodge and withdraw inward, would give them more information: "Why doesn't he show himself? Where is he hiding his enthusiasm? Why does he keep disappearing?"

Three boss/Five subordinate: Needing to be recognized, Threes can feel undervalued by subordinates who want to work alone and don't voice their support. Their commitment may indeed be only partial. But the Three's work pace can push Fives to the brink of exhaustion.
Three boss/Five subordinate: The more you do, the more the Three boss will ask for. No breaks, breakneck pace. The Three boss's desire for recognition can be lost on Fives.

Three boss/Five subordinate: The Three will feel disrespected, and the Five will feel obligated to fake some show of interest. Fives hate being used for others' benefit and would rather withdraw than waste their energy. Ideally, the Three boss should set up a program letting the Five subordinate know exactly what is expected of them.

Three boss/Five subordinate: Fives are willing to carry a heavy load if they know its exact weight and the distance to cover. Five bosses often struggle with the extroverted side of Three subordinates. Assigning Achievers to outward-facing missions, such as sales or marketing, can work well, but it will not suppress their desire to be valued by management.

Five boss/Three subordinate: Besides, Threes are ambitious and Fives hate intrusion. Since Five bosses like to retreat into an office and subordinates need a good reason to come disturb them, frustration will quickly build on both sides. Fives often adopt the appearance of a Three at the office.

Five boss/Three subordinate: An extroverted posture lets them function by playing a carefully rehearsed professional role. They lead with confidence when operating within the reassuring limits of a predetermined goal; they spend their time and energy generously when their attention is focused on their tasks rather than on themselves. Five bosses will need to be explicit in their dealings with Threes.

Five boss/Three subordinate: Hints and overly subtle messages will not work. Precise definitions of their role and of what is expected of them will help calm the Three's need to become the favorite. If the goal to be reached is clearly defined, the Three can turn out to be a flawless executor, combining the best of this kind of pairing — namely, the Five's analytical quality and the Three's driving dynamism.
Three boss/Five subordinate: The Three boss's desire for recognition can be lost on Fives.
Three boss/Five subordinate: The Three will feel disrespected, and the Five will feel obligated to fake some show of interest.

duos.title: Pair 3–6 (Three and Six)
amour: The Achiever–Loyalist couple in love The success of this pairing depends on easing the tension between performance and performance anxiety. Threes are drivers, and the key to their relationships lies in their ability to hit "Pause." Having to stop and talk about the relationship heightens the Three's anxiety about their own worth.

Frightened by the expression of feelings, the Three risks speeding up just when the Six, more inclined to turn inward, would want to stop and talk about their doubts. A reasonably mature Six will arrange for discussions of emotional themes to coincide with periods of shared activity. The Three partner will be reassured that bringing up feelings does not signal the end of all pleasures, nor of the joys their work brings them.

For Sixes, the key idea is being able to "move toward." Toward success, toward pleasure, toward trust in the other. In their relationship, this couple will move back and forth along the 3-6 axis of the Enneagram's central triangle.

This means the Three doubts their own emotions, and the Six is stressed by performance. The partners are positioned to help each other quite substantially. Threes are afraid of being in a relationship with someone whose worldview centers on doubt.

Sixes question the projected images and doubt the successes on which Threes rely to feel good. Threes can grow sad seeing their Six partners cyclically return to their outsider stance. Paradoxically, Achievers, in trying to encourage Loyalists to do their best, can become the object of paranoid scrutiny.

Sixes are stressed by the Three's position. Social visibility feels to them like a trap. Being socially visible exposes you to criticism and ridicule, which explains why the well-intentioned efforts of Three partners are often perceived as tricks or tests — which only heightens the Six's performance anxiety further.

Threes should give up achievement as the measure of their self-worth and instead turn their attention to the feelings underlying the Six's doubts. The Three could revise their definition of success by discovering various interesting facets of their loved one's personality. In the meantime, if the Three keeps dismissing the Six partner's recurring doubts as stupid and unjustified, this will signal their own inability to probe and acknowledge their own anxiety.

For their part, Sixes are regularly disappointed by what they perceive as boastfulness in Threes. In this couple, the partners conceive of success in markedly different ways. Threes feel energized when they have a mission to accomplish, while Sixes are amnesiac about their own successes and must be constantly reassured.

Threes see themselves as champions when they reach their goals, while Sixes doubt their own victory and go back to square one in terms of confidence. It would be good for Sixes to learn to focus on what they need to accomplish without letting doubt undermine them. By dismissing the Three's performance abilities as superficial, Sixes prove their own inability to focus on their goals.
This means the Three doubts their own emotions, and the Six is stressed by performance.
travail: The most natural alignment of talents has the Six generating original ideas and the Three shaping them into form.
Loyalists can chew on a complex idea for as long as it takes to perfect the theory and prepare the ground for the new product.
The Six's creative powers are generally sharpened by adversity, and they can do quite well without immediate recognition.
Threes are especially talented at promoting well-thought-out concepts.
They have a good "feel" for the market and know how to adapt products to consumer tastes.
When paired at the same level, the Six will often end up in a position solving problems, generating ideas, and designing good products that the Three can promote and sell.
hierarchie: Three boss/Six subordinate: The Three boss will need to respect the Six subordinate's contributions. Threes are known for claiming good ideas as their own, without regard for the contribution of those who brought them.

Three boss/Six subordinate: If the Six expects to be credited for a project and that recognition doesn't materialize, the superior will seem untrustworthy to them. The boss's leadership qualities will then be perceived as serving only their own interests, with no regard for subordinates.

Three boss/Six subordinate: The Six's suspicions of the Three should be defused before Six subordinates concoct a "disaster scenario" about the project's future. It is essential that bosses remember to give each person their due, especially those to whom the project's conceptualization is owed.

Three boss/Six subordinate: Sixes can be jealous guardians of their intellectual contributions and will often want those, above any other token of recognition, to be appreciated at their true worth. Once Sixes are assured their merits are recognized and they hold the place they deserve in the project's advancement, the Three boss can retake center stage.

Three boss/Six subordinate: If Threes set feelings aside and fail to notice rising rumors about their opportunism, Sixes are capable of adopting a victim stance and rallying other employees. Bosses should take account of the movement and recognize that it probably stems from the base of their company and not merely from one dissatisfied Six.

Three boss/Six subordinate: Threes too often tend to ignore negative messages, which breeds staff resentment. To take advantage of their possible shift toward the Six point of the Enneagram, Threes could question their certainty of being popular leaders and adopt the Six habit of doubting regularly.

Six boss/Three subordinate: A Six boss might seem overly cautious and overly bound to the rulebook in the eyes of an ambitious Three subordinate. For fear of losing control of the situation, the Six risks focusing on possible negative intentions without regard for the positive aspects of competition and personal initiative.

Six boss/Three subordinate: The Three subordinate will not really appreciate being ignored, and will not hesitate to look for a new job if a project offers no prospects for advancement. Threes flourish in an environment conducive to rapid growth and expansion, which runs counter to the Six boss's ambivalence about visibility.

Six boss/Three subordinate: If they want to make the most of sharing an Enneagram axis with them, Sixes should dare to take more risks. Besides, rather than controlling their employees' loyalty through rules, Six bosses could venture into the notions of image and efficiency so prized by Threes.
Three boss/Six subordinate: Bosses should take account of the movement and recognize that it probably stems from the base of their company and not merely from one dissatisfied Six.

duos.title: Pair 3–7 (Three and Seven)
amour: The Achiever–Epicure couple in love An energetic pairing that can produce a string of successful adventures. If the couple shares the same interests, the Three's ability to reach the goal complements rather well the Seven's multi-option mind. As long as projects keep multiplying, there will be no complaints of depression or boredom — but this couple might not spend much time together.

Unless they narrow their interests to a shared goal, the two partners could well end up trading news only on weekends! Both may overvalue the good sides of their relationship and slide past its flaws. There is no point dwelling on financial problems or raising the children when tomorrow's agenda or next year's plans are on one's mind.

Sensational ideas paired with sufficient means can make for a happy life, whatever it costs. Partners can keep silent about their own difficulties, and might not even be aware of them. Limits provoke a headlong rush forward.

Threes give themselves the illusion that everything is for the best and work relentlessly to avoid failure. Sevens avoid worrying and try to rationalize failure by imagining a better future. The neglect that can accumulate leaves this couple vulnerable to "surprising and unforeseen" problems, such as a financial situation turning critical or a child's grievances.

Some believe it is easy to spot Threes and Sevens, because they like themselves. Loving oneself boosts confidence. One expects to impress the other, because one is oneself impressed by one's own personality.

On the other hand, a good self-image has the drawback of making one somewhat superficial. It is hard to observe oneself long enough to notice one has taken a wrong step. Both profiles vanish when their public image is called into question: Threes change their image and start dressing up reality; Sevens change course and try to justify the change.

In matters of personal development, there is a kind of conspiracy to leave the other to steer their own course, rather than helping each other. Anxiety rises in each partner as emotions grow denser. Threes grow anxious when their love intensifies and their work slows down, because repressed feelings resurface, while Sevens fear losing their options and feeling trapped in a single commitment.

A mature couple will confront these anxieties rather than drowning them under a flood of activity. If they follow this path, Threes will find they can be just as effective at conquering the anxieties born of their relationship as at reaching a professional goal. A first step toward shedding their fear of emotional commitment is to set short-term goals, such as treating themselves to the pleasure of a weekly sauna together, or taking two hours a week to photograph each other.

For their part, Sevens are quite capable of making a relationship enjoyable. Concepts like pleasure and multiple choices can be a relief to Threes, who seek to look good rather than to feel good. Since Threes don't feel much while they're working to be recognized, the Seven's invitation to take pleasure and open up to different possibilities is a real windfall.

"Old" couples of this kind feel they have lived through all sorts of productive joys together. The Seven partner has developed stability around their goals, and, at the same time, the Three's inclination toward productivity has become a pleasure.
travail: This pairing often flourishes at the start of a project and comes apart before its completion. Threes and Sevens are two fairly close profiles.

They share the same drive at work and sustain their interest by widening the scope of their activities. Focusing their attention on the future, Sevens produce interesting syntheses of the many options on offer, and Threes turn the resources at hand into successes.

Each is capable of having several projects underway, or of working on different applications of the same project. Threes are fixated on their success and will even accept boring work to reach their ends.
The work itself matters, but a prestigious title and financial rewards are essential. Sevens are less concerned with the financial side.

Good competitors, attractive in appearance, they are often found alongside Threes at the head of the pack. Sevens resemble Threes and act like them, except that their professional motivation places adventure before achievement.
They like new and exciting jobs and would rather forgo a promotion that would limit their freedom of action.
The work itself matters, but a prestigious title and financial rewards are essential.
Sevens are less concerned with the financial side.
Good competitors, attractive in appearance, they are often found alongside Threes at the head of the pack.
Sevens resemble Threes and act like them, except that their professional motivation places adventure before achievement.
hierarchie: Three boss/Seven subordinate: Three bosses easily, and wrongly, mistake the enthusiasm of their Seven subordinates for a desire to grind through work. Representatives of both profiles perform well at work, but tend to take shortcuts, which can hurt the excellence of their output. Three bosses have goals and want results; efficiency can then take precedence over quality.

Three boss/Seven subordinate: As subordinates, Sevens also take shortcuts, but to avoid boredom. They are generally interested in work processes and will devote part of their time to discussing their ideas, trying them out, and getting them accepted. Threes take the lead, and Sevens try to smooth over authority.

Three boss/Seven subordinate: Wanting to expand the base of operations, Threes delegate more and more responsibility, which encourages the co-leadership principle so dear to Sevens. A common problem requiring mediation arises when Threes move forward, believing commitments have been honored, when in fact Sevens had steered clear of the boring phases of a project. Not remotely intimidated by hierarchy, Sevens can change how they do things without realizing they are acting entirely on their own initiative.

Three boss/Seven subordinate: Ideally, the boss should personally supervise the work done by their Seven subordinate during the final phase of a project. It is essential that everyone's responsibilities be clearly defined. Seven subordinates are generally happy to know who is officially in charge of them, but they will tend to work around authority to preserve their freedom.

Seven boss/Three subordinate: Seven bosses are always inspiring and popular during the early phases of a project. Successful Sevens like to delegate their powers once everything is in place. They then take on communication and promotion functions and only take back the reins to deal with urgent, temporary bottlenecks.

Seven boss/Three subordinate: Three subordinates can be excellent collaborators in seeing projects through. They want goals to be reached, and if Seven bosses are precise and practical, their directives will be followed to the letter. In this Three-Seven pairing, the most frequent dysfunction comes from two differing perceptions of the goal.

Seven boss/Three subordinate: Besides, Sevens who have trouble delegating generally leave gaps in the execution of their projects. They alter plans and issue new directives that subordinates sometimes find hard to follow. A Seven boss might not notice that the frustrated Three has been forced to take on leadership to make the Seven's instructions more coherent.

Seven boss/Three subordinate: If leadership is exercised irregularly or arises from a misunderstanding, the Three will step in and fill the gaps left by authority. When Threes are respected according to their own criteria of pay and recognition, the Three-Seven pairing works well. Sevens should give Threes titles and specific functions rather than handing over power to them.
Three boss/Seven subordinate: Not remotely intimidated by hierarchy, Sevens can change how they do things without realizing they are acting entirely on their own initiative.
Three boss/Seven subordinate: Ideally, the boss should personally supervise the work done by their Seven subordinate during the final phase of a project.

duos.title: Pair 3–8 (Three and Eight)
amour: The Achiever–Protector couple in love A fairly rare couple in our Enneagram experience. Both profiles are used to taking the active role in a relationship: Eights want to protect, and Threes want to keep the couple running smoothly.

Eights take control and deny their tender feelings, while Threes work at ignoring what they feel. The exercise of power is present in both partners, but neither is used to taking their emotional realm into account.
As a result, a breakthrough in the relationship often occurs when one of the partners goes through a failure. Three-Eight couples testify that some misfortune brought them closer together.

The Three notices that the Eight stayed by their side even when their image was tarnished; the Eight was moved when the Three found a way to save the situation in a difficult moment. When circumstances are favorable, the partners confide in each other.
Reassured about their own abilities and about the other's, they are destined for success. Threes should, nonetheless, learn to be more attuned to their partner's qualities.

They tend to believe they are the only one stepping up, when in fact, in love, Eights are often as generous as the altruism of Twos. Eights need attention and want to be reassured when their tough-guy armor starts to crack.
This couple comes together through action, but the realm of feelings remains to be discovered. A bond forged in action is entirely different from one formed through feelings.
The Eight's sensitivity develops when they can safely give up control of the relationship; the Three's blossoms when they feel loved for who they are and not for what they bring.
Reassured about their own abilities and about the other's, they are destined for success.
Threes should, nonetheless, learn to be more attuned to their partner's qualities.
travail: Threes and Eights both have a strong capacity for leadership. Endowed with strong assertiveness, they also both have a sense of territory.

They place more importance on productivity than on process and are furious when activity stops, for whatever reason. It is an unbeatable team in action when they're on the same side — but watch out for the power struggle if they're not on the same side!
The Eight's style is direct and confrontational. Nothing about them is hidden.
Threes are more the chameleon type. They adapt to every situation in order to be liked.
Eights build a solid launch pad, set a goal, and they're off. Threes are craftier: they get moving, work out a strategy using every available means, and test the waters.
As opponents, they fight to gain the upper hand. Threes consider Eights to be bullies, and Eights consider Threes to be liars.
Threes are more the chameleon type.
They adapt to every situation in order to be liked.
Eights build a solid launch pad, set a goal, and they're off.
Threes are craftier: they get moving, work out a strategy using every available means, and test the waters.
hierarchie: Eight boss/Three subordinate: The most common combination has the Eight in charge and the Three as the productivity champion in their area of activity. If the Three feels appreciated, the pairing will thrive.

Eight boss/Three subordinate: The Three wants their efforts rewarded in tangible ways, and the Eight boss, if wise, will honor this request rather than try to control it. Eight bosses distrust those who challenge their power, and Threes are exactly the type to do so.
Eight boss/Three subordinate: It would therefore be good for salary and status to be clearly defined. In any case, Threes will seize opportunities to climb the ladder.

Eight boss/Three subordinate: All will go well if the company's structure has the means to channel their ambitions. Three bosses will need to be fair, because Eights will wonder: "Can you trust a chameleon?", "Is the boss being fair to the staff?"
Three boss/Eight subordinate: Eight subordinates will challenge authority to get ahead of their worries: "Will he betray me when the time comes?" "Is the boss honest?
Three boss/Eight subordinate: Let's find out!" Eights can stir up trouble within the company, and bosses will have to put down a rebellion.
Three boss/Eight subordinate: The central question concerns the integrity of management. Eights can only invest themselves fully if they feel safe.

Three boss/Eight subordinate: Three bosses would do well to confirm to Eight subordinates what positions they might aspire to later on. Eights, too, need to know what the company has planned for their future.
Three boss/Eight subordinate: Eight subordinates will challenge authority to get ahead of their worries: "Will he betray me when the time comes?"
Three boss/Eight subordinate: "Is the boss honest?

duos.title: Pair 3–9 (Three and Nine)
amour: The Achiever–Mediator couple in love Achievers want to impress their partner, and Nines tend to merge with the other's ideas. This pattern will encourage the Three to project an image that will win the Nine over. Happy for the attention paid to them, the Nine will be tempted to support the Three's momentum and to ease their understanding by accepting that the notion of a goal is central to this couple. The Nine, in search of a purpose in life, may become enthralled by their partner's goals.

The other's ideas seem more invigorating than their own priorities, which remain poorly defined. As a result, the Nine finds themselves caught up in the partner's concerns, sometimes for a long time. The impressionable Nine may try to play up their social image, like the Three, and think, "That's it, I've found myself, I've finally discovered what to do with my life." The Three-Nine couple shares one of the Enneagram's axes, and this axis holds that the Mediator finds security by adopting an image and a professional identity.

A productive existence, driven by the Three and shared by the Nine, can come about provided the goals defined by the Three take into account the Nine's neglected inner needs. The Three-Nine axis of the Enneagram also suggests that Threes feel uncomfortable with inaction. Stressed Threes fall into the same uncertainty about their goals that is typical of Nines, and then feel unproductive. Difficulty making choices produces a kind of lethargy, unpleasant for both partners.

Nines dread the overwhelming drop in energy that occurs when they no longer have to mobilize, and Threes will then rush to find new priorities so there is always something to do. If the Nine stops following the partner's priorities to guide their choices, they can sink into a routine resembling sleepwalking. They express their dissatisfaction by cutting back their energy output and limiting themselves to mechanical activities. They may not openly voice their refusal, but will have put their presence and enthusiasm to sleep.

The relationship will be in crisis without much having been said. Family life will go on, with the Three busy with outside activities and the Nine dozing off. The Three will work a great deal, and the Nine, often with just as full a schedule, will run on the minimum energy needed to keep up the bare routine. Neither will be ready to admit there is a problem.

The Three will keep working "for the couple," and the Nine will keep themselves busy to numb their disappointment and anger. Nines, who feel reluctantly dragged along in pursuit of their partner's goals, will eventually start asking themselves questions like: "How did we get here?", "Did I really choose this path?", "Do I even belong here?" These questions can become obsessive if the Three's priorities truly dominate the couple's life. Their minds clouded by these inner questions, Nines grow stressed the way Sixes do, question the validity of their relationship, but have difficulty proposing solutions.

Achievers will be irritated if the Nine's questioning ends up disrupting family life. Lacking other solutions, it is generally the Three who reacts, either by burying themselves in work, or by starting another romantic relationship, or by taking the initiative for a change. Threes are often eager to encourage "constructive changes," especially if their "productive support" increases the couple's chances of success. The couple would need to understand that the Nine's need to find themselves is, in fact, a priority for both partners.

It is too easy for Threes to view this quest for inner direction as self-pity; growing impatient at the idea of wasting time on existential questions rather than devoting one's days to action will not help Threes grow. "Why stir up problems when so many short-term projects are calling? Why search for deep motivations when they only create discomfort?" The search for one's inner identity should instead awaken the Three who, like a chameleon, manages to be accepted by projecting an appropriate image.

At best, the Three will welcome this process and wish for the Nine's flourishing, but will still wonder: "Why is this taking so long?" It is interesting to note that Nines who eventually find an identity may never change careers or consider a separation. Instead, they feel fully reintegrated into the life they had already built, "a life I've made my own since discovering that I wanted it."
The Three-Nine axis of the Enneagram also suggests that Threes feel uncomfortable with inaction.
travail: The sheer volume of the Three's activity can become the norm in a company.
Their energetic profile suits professional life, and Nines are quite admiring of people who fulfill themselves through their work.

By modeling the positive aspects of the Three's professional persona, Nines end up developing habits that further their careers; they manage to pace themselves according to deadlines and thereby stabilize the energy they expend.
Nines generally appreciate the characteristics of their security point.

They may look and act like Threes, with, however, certain essential differences: Nines will keep considering every aspect of a problem, will readily fall in with someone else's goals, and will avoid conflict.
From the Three's point of view, these tendencies slow the pace, whereas Nines feel that taking different opinions into account proves, on the contrary, that one runs one's business with heart.
hierarchie: Three boss/Nine subordinate: Three bosses tend to keep expanding their sphere of influence. As soon as one deal is finalized, it's high time to move on to the next.

Three boss/Nine subordinate: Getting the Three boss's attention will be difficult, unless the matter concerns the project — which pushes other subjects, like ethics or internal organization, indefinitely into the future. Nines themselves may recognize it isn't professional to spend too much time on office politics, but they will still be sensitive to staff discontent that a Three boss won't even have noticed.

Three boss/Nine subordinate: Threes often find excuses to stay out of quarrels and become aggressive if those quarrels hinder the smooth running of the company. Their goal is always to move forward, and they may go so far as to treat their subordinates as mere objects, useful or not.

Three boss/Nine subordinate: It can seem logical to drop people of no value and encourage those who have some. An inexperienced Three boss treats employees according to what they can bring to the company.

Three boss/Nine subordinate: Nines could be the first to feel threatened; and since they are called upon to keep the peace, they could be among the last to voice an opinion. Slipping into opposition, Nines will analyze the different aspects of the problem and indirectly express their discontent, managing to obstruct the course of action the Three boss has asked for.
Nine boss/Three subordinate: The indecisiveness of a Nine boss can destabilize subordinates who are oriented toward a goal. Threes find thorough research pointless.

Nine boss/Three subordinate: It seems to them that gathering data, rather than making decisions easier, is gradually becoming an end in itself. Too much information overloads the system, and it is frustrating to think that results could be called into question in light of conflicting viewpoints.

Nine boss/Three subordinate: Three subordinates want precise, near-term goals, and Nine bosses see how these goals might shift depending on circumstances. Their differing ways of seeing things can lead to a situation where the Three subordinate wants a project wrapped up, while the Nine boss is still poring over feasibility reports.
Nine boss/Three subordinate: The intervention of a third party can prove extremely useful. Ideally, each should be able to perceive the positive aspects of the other's strategy.

Nine boss/Three subordinate: Nines should be able to set priorities, make comparisons, and understand the merit of more assertive leadership. Threes should be able to wait, appreciate others' opinions, and relate everyone's needs to their level of productivity.

duos.title: Pair 4–4 (Four and Four)
amour: A couple of Romantics in love Although Romantics love going out together and often become friends, I have known few Four couples. A shared pastime often explains the friendship between two Fours. They go to the opera together, go jogging, and talk about their relationships. They cry, dress well, argue, and make up quickly.

Very good friends who share the same worldview confirm each other's worth, which helps them neutralize their underlying shame at not being good enough to deserve love. Very good friends can also afford to be more frank and open with each other than actual couples tend to be. Fours are, in fact, convinced that if they revealed a serious fault to their partner, they would risk being abandoned. Fours as a couple are bound together by an intense aesthetic sensitivity, tenderness, and acceptance of each other's mood swings.

A good couple relationship is steeped in the whole range of feelings. How could happiness be authentic without feeling what its loss would be? Doesn't a loving bond have separation and sadness as its counterparts? Fours as a couple can place tremendous importance on the search for a deeply satisfying relationship.
Mere affection, by comparison, feels like a shallow comedy. "A real relationship should become an artistic achievement." "How can other couples settle for so little? Where do they find enchantment?

That could never happen to us!" Fours sometimes fail to help each other because each overvalues their own sensitivity. They may well imagine the danger posed by exaggerated expectations, but for them, questioning the quest for absolute love would amount to devaluing it. Romantics' needs are highly idealized; a couple's relationship cannot result in a permanent state of absolute happiness.

Moments of ecstasy are fleeting, and if one asks too much of them, something will always seem to be missing. Whatever is missing from the Four's happiness makes them lose their sense of proportion. Their house is never big enough, their partner never ardent enough, their salaries never generous enough, and their coffee never sweet enough. The relationship can become the main source of dissatisfaction, with years spent insisting that the partner needs to change.

"I can't bear the thought of leaving you, and I can't send you away either; if you satisfied me, I wouldn't be the same person, so you are responsible for my unhappiness." Needless to say, blame is an integral part of their relationship as a couple. On the negative side, each suffers and considers the other responsible, each wants the other to be a perfect lover, and each feels flawed. They blame each other for their shortcomings and try to dodge when their own are pointed out.
